bib.title: A Diverse Corpus for Evaluating and Developing English Math Word Problem Solvers
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 975-984

read.skipped: Figures 1-7 are images; only captions read.

question: How can an English math word problem corpus be built and measured so that it reflects the true capability of MWP solvers rather than exaggerating it through repeated patterns?
hypothesis: Low lexicon diversity in a corpus inflates solver accuracy, so a more diverse corpus gives a more faithful measure.
contributions: A diverse (lexicon usage), wide-coverage (problem type), publicly available MWP corpus with annotations (ASDiv).
A lexicon usage diversity metric to measure the diversity of an MWP corpus, used to evaluate existing corpora.
Evidence that real performance of SOTA systems is far behind human performance when evaluated on a corpus that mimics a real human test.

method.summary: ASDiv collects 2,305 MWPs from 28 websites, pruning or revising items too similar to existing ones under a BLEU-based lexicon diversity metric, and annotates problem type, equation, answer and grade level. Three solvers (LCA++, UnitDep, GTS) are run on MathQA-C, ASDiv-A and ASDiv with 5-fold cross-validation to show accuracy falls as corpus lexicon diversity rises.
method.task: English math word problem solving (benchmark construction and corpus diversity measurement)

datasets.name: ASDiv
datasets.split: 5-fold cross-validation, split per problem type into five nearly equal subsets
datasets.source: collected from 28 websites; annotated by one master-degree research assistant; public at github.com/chao-chun/nlu-asdiv-dataset
datasets.preprocessing: MWPs highly similar to existing ones (by LD metric) pruned or revised; equation-answer consistency checked by program, inconsistent ones re-annotated; 480 random samples (20 per problem type) checked and all correct

datasets.name: ASDiv-A
datasets.preprocessing: only arithmetic operations, no external constants, no reused operands

datasets.name: MathQA-C
datasets.source: from 4,117 arithmetic MathQA MWPs (Amini et al. 2019)
datasets.preprocessing: arithmetic-only, no external constants or reused operands, inconsistent problems filtered out

datasets.name: MathQA
datasets.split: official train/test used for diversity analysis
datasets.preprocessing: arithmetic subset checked with SymPy; 27% of annotated formulas do not match labeled answers

models.name: GTS (Xie and Sun, 2019)
models.architecture: neural, two-layer gate-feedforward networks, goal-driven tree-structured

other.note: Existing solvers are trained as in their original papers; no hyperparameters are given. GTS experiment repeated 5 times and averaged.

inference.samples: 5-fold cross-validation; GTS repeated 5 times and averaged

parameters.LD n-gram order: BLEU bi-directional, n-grams up to n=4
parameters.LD normalisation: Stanford CoreNLP tokenise and POS tag, NLTK lemmatise, stop word removal, named entity and quantity replaced by meta symbols
parameters.LD histogram: uniformly quantized into 20 intervals between 0 and 1

metrics.name: Lexicon usage diversity LD_i
metrics.definition: 1 - max over j!=i of (BLEU(P_i,P_j)+BLEU(P_j,P_i))/2, among MWPs of the same problem type

metrics.name: Corpus lexicon diversity (CLD)
metrics.definition: mean of all LD_i in the corpus

metrics.name: Syntactic pattern diversity SD_i
metrics.definition: same as LD on POS sequences

metrics.name: Answer accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of MWPs whose solver answer is correct, 5-fold cross-validation

eval.protocol: 5-fold cross-validation; significance marked p<0.01 for ASDiv-A and ASDiv vs MathQA-C for GTS (test not named)

evidence.quote: a new English MWP corpus with 2,305 MWPs

results.claim: The best solver accuracy on ASDiv is only about 36%, far below human performance.
results.setup: LCA++, UnitDep, GTS on ASDiv (CLD 0.49), 5-fold CV
results.quote: the overall performance is only around 36% on ASDiv
results.note: Table 3 prints 0.36, 0.37, 0.36 for L, U, G.

results.table: Table 3, row G, columns MathQA-C and ASDiv-A (0.86, 0.68)
results.note: L and U fail ('-') on MathQA-C. On ASDiv-A L=0.68, U=0.78.

results.claim: CLD of MathQA across the whole corpus is only 0.05, with LD=0 for 85% of its MWPs.
results.quote: Figure 1 shows that its CLD is only 0.05.

results.claim: 27% of arithmetic MathQA problems have annotated formulas that do not match the labeled answer.
results.setup: MathQA arithmetic subset, formulas solved with SymPy

results.claim: Percentage of MWPs with LD=0 (identical after normalisation): MathQA 85%, IL 28%, AI2 22%, ALGES 20%, ASDiv none.
results.setup: per-corpus, within problem type where annotated
results.quote: there are about 85%, 28%, 22% and 20% identical MWPs

results.claim: Accuracy falls sharply at grades 5 and 6 on ASDiv.

results.table: Table 4, row G, columns G1 (0.64) and G6 (0.01)

results.claim: CLD for MathQA-C is 0.08 and for ASDiv-A 0.50; LD=0 for 82% of MathQA-C.
results.quote: The CLDs for MathQA-C and ASDiv-A were found to be 0.08 and 0.50, respectively.

results.claim: MathQA has the highest train-test CLD (0.85) but a low within-test CLD (0.27) versus 0.57 for ASDiv.
results.setup: MathQA official test set within-test CLD vs ASDiv-A and ASDiv means
results.quote: the CLD=0.27 of MathQA measured within the test set is actually low

results.claim: Share of MWPs with SD_i=0 (identical POS patterns): MathQA 87%, IL 54%, AI2 46%, ALGES 33%, ASDiv 4%.
48% of ASDiv-A MWPs have LD >= 0.5 vs 7% for MathQA-C.
results.quote: the lexicon diversity indices of 48% of the MWPs in our ASDiv-A are larger than or equal to 0.5

limits: Only three solvers, all arithmetic-only, tested; ASDiv-A used for the comparison with MathQA-C.
Correlation of CLD with accuracy is shown on two or three corpora, not a controlled test; corpora also differ in size and problem types.
Annotation by a single research assistant; human-level performance not measured, only asserted as higher.
Test used for significance not named; GTS hyperparameters not given.
Dated: pre-LLM solvers; no LLM or prompting evaluation.
